title: Supreme Court sets aside High Court order for CBI, ED checks on Rahul Gandhi's assets
dek: The Allahabad High Court must hear the case afresh, with the Leader of the Opposition as a party, including whether the BJP worker's complaint can be heard at all.
body:
The Supreme Court on Wednesday set aside orders of the Allahabad High Court that had directed the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the Enforcement Directorate (ED) to verify a complaint that Rahul Gandhi, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, holds assets beyond his known income. The case goes back to the High Court, which must now hear Mr Gandhi before passing any order against him.

The bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana disposed of Mr Gandhi's appeal and directed the High Court to consider the matter afresh on all issues, including whether the petition is maintainable at all, according to reports of the hearing. The written order had not been uploaded to the court's website by Wednesday evening.

## The complaint

The case was brought by S Vignesh Shishir, a BJP worker from Karnataka, who alleged that Mr Gandhi and his family hold assets disproportionate to their income and asked for an investigation. In May, a division bench of the High Court's Lucknow bench directed that, if the complaint had been received, the allegations be verified in accordance with law, that the CBI or ED could take any lawful steps based on that verification, and that both agencies report their progress to the court.

In July the same bench, of Justices Rajesh Singh Chauhan and Brij Raj Singh, was critical of the CBI. "The counter affidavit of C.B.I. does not appear to be a counter affidavit in terms of earlier order," it said, and asked for a fresh affidavit from a senior officer explaining the progress of the inquiry. It accepted that the ED had taken the steps required, saying the agency "may not be helpless" if material emerged. It kept the records in a sealed cover and listed the case for August.

## Mr Gandhi's challenge

Mr Gandhi appealed to the Supreme Court. His lawyers argued that the complainant had no legal standing to bring the case, that he had not disclosed his credentials, and questioned how details of confidential procedures had appeared in newspapers, according to reports. Mr Gandhi had not been made a party before the High Court issued its directions.

On 17 August the Supreme Court asked the High Court to defer its proceedings, observing that the order had been passed without giving the Leader of the Opposition a chance to be heard, and told the CBI and ED not to file any report in response to the High Court's directions in the meantime.

## A separate citizenship case

The same complainant has also petitioned the High Court alleging that Mr Gandhi is a British citizen. In April the High Court ordered a police case to be registered against him in that matter, then stayed its own direction a day later. Wednesday's ruling does not deal with that case.

## Reactions and what happens next

Neither the Congress nor the BJP had issued a formal statement on the ruling by Wednesday evening.

The Allahabad High Court will now list the case again and must hear Mr Gandhi before deciding whether the complaint should go further. No date has been set. The ruling does not stop the CBI or ED from acting on the complaint under their own powers if the law allows, reports said, but the High Court's directions to them no longer stand.

This story is based on reports of the hearing and of the High Court's earlier orders; it will be updated when the Supreme Court's order is published.
